sections.name: CodeEntry
sections.title: Shape of a code explorer entry
sections.what: Describes one entry from the manifest: the repository name, a URL slug, the GitHub name, an optional link to a matching project page, visibility, a one-line summary, counts of files and sections, a readiness value, and whether a map is available.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared description means the server and browser pages read the manifest the same way.
sections.watch_out: The readiness field is plain text, not a fixed list, so a misspelled value passes the type check and appears wrong on screen.

sections.name: VERDICT
sections.title: Readiness labels for display
sections.what: Turns the four readiness codes into the words a visitor sees: Ready, Needs work, Not ready, and Not checked for unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: the manifest stores short codes, and this keeps the visible wording in one place so it can change without touching the data.
sections.watch_out: A code missing from this list gets no label, so the page may show nothing or the raw code, and the code does not say which.

summary: Defines the shape of one code explorer manifest entry and the readable labels for each readiness code.
purpose: Provides a shared type and label list for the code explorer, for both browser and server pages.
why: The file's comments say it is kept outside the browser component so server pages, such as the code index, can use the same type.
how: First, one entry shape is defined. Then the four readiness codes are mapped to labels that a visitor reads.
inputs: The manifest file written by the clarity tool, stored at public/code/manifest.json according to the comments.
outputs: Types and a label lookup. The file produces no output of its own.
risks: The readiness field is free text in the type, while the label list only knows four codes, so the two can drift apart. Optional fields such as the stale count and build date must be handled when missing.
debug: If a readiness label shows as a raw code, compare the readiness value in the manifest with the keys in the label list. If an explorer entry is missing or wrong, check that the manifest's fields and types match this entry shape.
